title: 854. Mirror Reflection

examples.explanation: After one bounce the ray arrives at sensor 2.
Parity puts the first hit on sensor 0.

hints: Unfold the bounces into a straight ray through tiled copies of the room; the hit happens when both coordinates are multiples of `p`.
Divide out common factors of two from `p` and `q`, then look at parity: an even unfolded `p` means sensor 2, else an even unfolded `q` means sensor 0, otherwise sensor 1.
The least common multiple of `p` and `q` tells how far the straight ray travels before aligning with corners.
